claim: The SIA/BCG 2021 study describes the semiconductor value chain as pre-competitive research, chip design, wafer fabrication (front end) and assembly, packaging and test (back end), supported by an ecosystem of EDA/core IP, equipment and materials suppliers.
evidence: "Chip design... develop the nanometer-scale integrated circuits which perform the critical tasks" (p. 15); "Wafer fabrication (front end manufacturing)... print the nanometer-scale integrated circuits from the chip design into silicon wafers" (p. 16); "Assembly, packaging & testing (back end manufacturing)... converting the silicon wafers produced by the fabs into finished chips" (p. 19); "Electronic design automation (EDA) companies provide sophisticated software and services to support designing semiconductors" (p. 19); "Semiconductor manufacturing also rely on specialized suppliers of materials" (p. 21)
notes: Sentences partly elided by the fetch tool ('...'); locations as reported.

claim: The 2021 US government supply-chain review split the semiconductor supply chain into five segments: design; fabrication; assembly, test and packaging (ATP) and advanced packaging; materials; and manufacturing equipment.
evidence: "This report examines the semiconductor supply chain through five related essential segments: (1) design; (2) fabrication; (3) assembly, test, and packaging (ATP) and advanced packaging; (4) materials; and (5) manufacturing equipment." (p. 22)

claim: Chip design consists of specification, logic design, physical design, and validation and verification.
evidence: "specification, logic design, physical design, and validation and verification" (p. 6)

claim: Assembly, testing and packaging starts by cutting a finished wafer into individual chips, mounting each chip on a frame with wires to connect it to external devices, and enclosing it in a protective casing.
evidence: "Assembly, testing, and packaging starts with cutting a finished wafer—which contains dozens of chips in a grid pattern after fabrication—into separate chips. Each chip is mounted on a frame with wires that connect the chip to external devices, and enclosed in a protective casing." (p. 7)

claim: In photolithography, light is passed through a photomask (a transparent plate carrying a circuit pattern) to transfer that pattern onto the photoresist on the wafer.
evidence: "A photolithography tool passes light through a 'photomask'—a transparent plate with a circuit pattern—to transfer that pattern to the photoresist." (p. 6)

claim: Chip fabrication and test use more than 50 different types of specialised wafer processing and testing equipment.
evidence: "more than 50 different types of sophisticated wafer processing and testing equipment" (p. 19)

claim: Fabs depend on thousands of upstream suppliers providing hundreds of chemical, gas and material inputs, each with its own supply chain.
evidence: "The supply chain required to fabricate chips is a globally integrated, complex network of thousands of upstream suppliers that provide fabs with hundreds of chemical, gas, and material inputs, each with precise requirements and their own sophisticated supply chains." (p. 2)

claim: SEMI describes silicon wafers as the fundamental building material for the majority of semiconductors.
evidence: "Silicon wafers are the fundamental building material for the majority of semiconductors, which are vital components of all electronic devices."

claim: Core IP consists of reusable modular portions of chip designs, and EDA is the software used to design chips.
evidence: Core IP: "reusable modular portions of designs" (p. 6); EDA: "software used to design chips" (p. 6)

claim: Design accounted for about 65% of total semiconductor industry R&D (2019, SIA/BCG estimate).
evidence: "Design activity is largely knowledge- and skill-intensive: it accounts for 65% of the total industry R&D and 53% of the value added" (p. 15)
